dedupe_keys.name: historical global map of nh4 and no3 application in synthetic nitrogen fertilizer 1961 2010

description: This dataset maps synthetic nitrogen fertilizer application on cropland at 0.5 by 0.5 degree resolution for 1961 to 2010, split into ammonium (NH4+) and nitrate (NO3-) forming inputs. The PANGAEA record says national consumption from FAOSTAT was gap-filled by multiple imputation (19 percent of national values were missing) using year, population, GDP and crop area, then downscaled to a gridded cropland map, and that global inputs rose from 15 to 110 Tg N over the period. It was published in 2017 by Kazuya Nishina, Akihiko Ito, Naota Hanasaki and Seiji Hayashi as a downloadable ZIP of NetCDF files of about 32.5 MB, free under CC BY 3.0, with global coverage. Caveats: values are downscaled national totals, not farm data, and imputed years carry extra uncertainty. For simulation it gives fertilizer input fields for crop, water quality and nutrient runoff models, and a demand proxy for fertilizer supply chain disruption scenarios. Related catalogue records include the half-degree nitrogen and phosphorus fertilizer use data and the UKCEH Land Cover plus Fertilisers for England.
